history.period: 1950 (kutiya and first idol); large Hanuman statue 1953; Shiv temple 1957
history.summary: Identity confirmed and kept DISTINCT from Hanuman Garhi, Ayodhya (seq 2367): this is the Neem Karoli Baba temple on a hilltop 3.5 km south of Tallital, Nainital. Built in 1950 by Neem Karoli Baba (a decade before his Kainchi Dham ashram) on a site that was then a children's graveyard avoided by locals; a kutiya and small Hanuman idol came first, then a large Hanuman statue in 1953 and a Shiv temple in 1957. The inner shrine depicts Hanuman tearing open his chest to reveal Rama and Sita in his heart; a huge outdoor Hanuman statue with a golden umbrella guards the complex. Shrines to Shiva, Rama, Krishna, Sheetala Mata and Neem Karoli Baba share the hill. It is Nainital's best-known sunrise/sunset viewpoint. Opening hours CONFLICT across sources (verify).

name: Hanuman Garhi
town_description: Nainital is a hill-station town in the Kumaon Himalayas at about 2,000 m, built around the mango-shaped Naini Lake. It is a major summer resort and pilgrimage town; the lake, Mall Road (Mallital/Tallital) and the Naina Devi temple on the lake's northern bank are its anchors.

travel.road: ~3.5 km south of Tallital bus stop on Haldwani Road, at 1,951 m; motorable to the base, then ~70 steps uphill
